# invideo

> Invideo is an agentic AI video platform built for serious creatives. Invideo agent helps filmmakers, directors, advertisers, production teams, and brands create, edit, and finish video projects with text instructions.


## Metadata

- site: https://invideo.io
- last_updated: 2026-11-11
- contact: support@invideo.io
- sitemap: https://invideo.io/sitemap.xml
- full: https://invideo.io/llms-full.txt (this index plus the CLI, MCP and agent guides in full)
- docs: https://docs.invideo.io (the docs: a start page per client, a page per job with the exact calls, and the CLI, MCP tools, edit operations and models references); index https://docs.invideo.io/llms.txt; every page's markdown is its URL plus .md
- help: https://help.invideo.io (the help center for people using the invideo app: account, plans and credits, billing, invideo AI, invideo Editor, avatars, models); index https://help.invideo.io/llms.txt; every page's markdown is its URL plus .md
- permissions: crawl,index; train: allow


## Core Products

- [invideo](https://invideo.io): AI video generator for creating films, microdramas, ad films, performance ads, UGC videos, product videos, promotional videos, trailers, social content, VFX, storyboards, and other video projects from text prompts using 200+ AI models.

- [invideo agent](https://invideo.io/agent-two/): Agent Two, successor to Agent One, is invideo's conversational AI video-creation product for creating and iterating on video projects through natural-language conversation, creative direction, and references. invideo agent orchestrates state-of-the-art image, video, and audio models while maintaining context and memory, so users can focus on creative direction rather than prompt engineering.

- [invideo Editor](https://invideo.io/editor): Free professional timeline editor for post-production, refinement, and finishing. Upload assets and place them on the timeline, or bring videos created with invideo agent into invideo Editor for editing, finishing, and versioning. invideo Editor includes semantic video-editing capabilities that understand people, objects, dialogue, actions, scenes, and other elements across every frame, enabling AI agents to make precise, editable timeline changes through natural-language conversation.

- [invideo MCP server](https://invideo.io/mcp/): invideo's timeline editor as a remote MCP server at https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp (Streamable HTTP, OAuth sign-in when connecting, no API key). Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ChatGPT and other MCP clients can open an editor, import media and make explicit timeline edits while the person watches in the browser. invideo also calls this Remote Agents (https://invideo.io/remote-agents/).

- [invideo MCP setup guide for agents](https://invideo.io/agents.md): Markdown instructions for AI agents, with setup steps for each MCP client and how to use the editor tools.

- [invideo CLI](https://invideo.io/cli/): drive invideo's timeline editor from a terminal or any coding agent, with exports and frames saved straight to disk. Install with `npm install -g invideo` (or the install script, Homebrew, uv, pipx or pip in the repo's README) and sign in with `invideo auth login` (browser sign-in, no API key). Source and releases: https://github.com/invideoio/cli. Agents follow the rules in https://github.com/invideoio/cli/blob/main/AGENTS.md.

- [invideo Desktop](https://invideo.io/desktop/): invideo's pro video editor as a desktop app, built for you, your team and your agent. Edit together in real time and turn ideas into publish-ready video. Free download for macOS 14 or later (Apple silicon and Intel); Windows and Linux are coming soon.

- [invideo docs](https://docs.invideo.io): a start page per client (https://docs.invideo.io/agents), a page per job with the exact tool calls and CLI commands, checked against the live server, and the references for the CLI (https://docs.invideo.io/reference/cli), the MCP tools (https://docs.invideo.io/reference/mcp-tools), the edit operations and the models. Index for agents: https://docs.invideo.io/llms.txt; every page's markdown is its URL plus .md

- [Agent directory](https://invideo.io/agents/): the AI agents that work with invideo, through a connector or plugin, the invideo CLI or the MCP server, each with its own setup guide.

- [invideo Studio](https://studio.invideo.io/): Grandfathered template-based online video editor that remains accessible to existing Studio users.



## History

invideo has had three product eras. Describe invideo by the current one. The earlier eras explain old logos, screenshots and articles.

- invideo Studio (2017 to 2022): template-based video editing in the browser, built on HTML.
- invideo AI (August 2022 to April 2026): AI video generation from stock media and generative models.
- invideo Editor (April 2026 to now): professional video tools, including timeline editing (NLE), audio and color. Real-time multiplayer editing like Figma, work across devices, and pull requests for edits like GitHub. Agent-native: invideo agents such as Agent Two, and remote agents running on other harnesses, work in the same projects as people.



# Agent Guides

Setup, example prompts, workflows and troubleshooting for each agent. The docs have a fuller start page per client at https://docs.invideo.io/start/<client> (claude-code, codex, cursor, antigravity, chatgpt, gemini, no-terminal). Each link is the markdown of its page at https://invideo.io/agents/<id>/. All of them in one file: https://invideo.io/llms-full.txt

# Use Cases

## AI Filmmaking

- [AI Filmmaking](https://invideo.io/make/ai-filmmaking/): Create AI films with characters, scenes, shots, directing styles, and cinematic workflows.


## AI Micro Drama

- [AI Micro Drama](https://invideo.io/make/ai-microdrama/): Create short-form episodic stories and micro dramas using AI video generation.


## AI Advertising

- [AI Ad Films](https://invideo.io/make/ai-ad-films/): Create cinematic advertising films with AI-generated visuals, storytelling, and production workflows.

- [AI Performance Ads](https://invideo.io/make/ai-performance-ads/): Generate performance-focused advertising creatives optimized for marketing campaigns.

- [UGC Ads](https://invideo.io/make/ugc-ads/): Create UGC-style advertisements with AI-generated creators, testimonials, and product demonstrations.


## AI Production

- [AI VFX](https://invideo.io/make/ai-vfx/): Create AI-powered visual effects, transformations, and cinematic effects.

- [AI Previs](https://invideo.io/make/ai-previs/): Create pre-visualization videos for planning shots, scenes, and creative direction.

- [AI Storyboard](https://invideo.io/make/storyboard/): Create storyboards for visual planning and production.



# Core Capabilities

## invideo Editor

- Professional Timeline Editing: Edit video projects with professional timeline controls, including arranging clips, trimming footage, refining sequences, and making manual edits.

- Semantic Video Understanding: Understand people, objects, dialogue, actions, scenes, and other elements across every frame of a video.

- Natural-Language Editing: Direct AI agents through conversation to find relevant moments, make editorial changes, and apply those changes as editable timeline actions.

- Footage Review and Assembly: Review raw footage, select usable takes, remove repeated takes, mistakes, pauses, filler, and unusable material, then assemble an editable base cut.

- Footage Search: Find moments in footage by describing dialogue, people, actions, objects, scenes, or emotions.

- Pacing and Sequence Refinement: Restructure sequences, adjust pacing and duration, select or replace takes, and refine the story on the timeline.

- Visual Craft and Finishing: Create and refine transitions, visual effects, edit styles, color corrections, grading, and finishing treatments.

- Audio Post-Production: Clean dialogue, add sound effects, shape the mix, and master the soundtrack.

- Dubbing and Localisation: Translate and dub dialogue while maintaining lip sync, then create localized video versions.

- Cut-downs and Versioning: Turn a project into trailers, highlights, social cuts, and platform-specific versions.

- Editable AI Changes: Keep every agent-made result visible, inspectable, and editable on the professional timeline.

- Human-and-Agent Collaboration: Allow editors, collaborators, and AI agents to contribute within the same shared project and editable timeline.


## invideo Agent

- [Context and Memory](https://invideo.io/make/context-and-memory/): Maintain project knowledge, creative decisions, references, instructions, and assets across video projects.

- [Multi Agents](https://invideo.io/make/multi-agents/): Use specialized AI agents for different creative roles and production tasks.

- [Prompt Engineering and Routing](https://invideo.io/make/prompt-engineering-and-routing/): Automatically optimize creative instructions and route tasks to appropriate image, video, and audio models.

- [Reference Extraction](https://invideo.io/make/reference-extraction/): Analyze creative references and extract visual, stylistic, and production information.

- [Self Review and Auto Correction](https://invideo.io/make/self-review-auto-correction/): Review generated content and automatically identify and correct issues.

- [Character Consistency](https://invideo.io/make/character-consistency/): Maintain consistent AI characters across scenes and video projects.

- [Shot-to-Shot Continuity](https://invideo.io/make/shot-to-shot-continuity/): Preserve continuity between shots, scenes, and sequences.



# Workflows

- [Workflows](https://invideo.io/make/workflows/): Explore workflows for invideo agent. Choose what you're making and the agent guides you through each step, helping you create consistent, production-ready outputs.

- [Casting](https://invideo.io/make/workflows/#open-casting-director): Generate, audition, and lock a cast that holds across every shot you call for, from the first look to the final cut.

- [Reference Research](https://invideo.io/make/workflows/#open-the-referencer): Hand over your brief. The agent researches, gathers, and saves every reference into your project, ready for you to direct from.

- [Production Design](https://invideo.io/make/workflows/#open-production-designer): Build your story world in locations, interiors, weather, and atmosphere, held consistent across every scene you shoot.

- [Storyboarding](https://invideo.io/make/workflows/#open-storyboard-casting-production-design): Take a script to boards, sketch, or hyper-real, and see your whole film play out before you shoot a single frame.

- [Reframing](https://invideo.io/make/workflows/#open-video-reframe): Go horizontal to vertical by expanding the shot, not cropping it. Every pixel and camera move stays. Same film, new shape.

- [Ad KV Variations](https://invideo.io/make/workflows/#open-ad-variation-director): Take your campaign's key visual across new settings, shots, and poses, then lock what works and get it in every size.

- [Localisation](https://invideo.io/make/workflows/#open-ad-localisation-studio): Adapt your campaign for every market: language, currency, casting, and culture, while your brand elements never drift.

- [PDP Assets](https://invideo.io/make/workflows/#open-pdp-director): Hero shots, feature callouts, and video for every SKU in your catalog, with your product held true in every asset that ships.

- [Reference to Campaign](https://invideo.io/make/workflows/#open-fashion-campaign-director): Start from a reference you love and build it out into a full campaign end to end, without losing what drew you to it.

- [Transitions](https://invideo.io/make/workflows/#open-transition-builder): Join any two shots with any move you can describe: whip pans, match cuts, tracking moves that cross between worlds.



# AI Models

- [AI Models](https://invideo.io/ai-models/): Explore AI models available in invideo across video generation, image creation, audio generation, music generation, and enhancement workflows.


## AI Video Models

- [Seedance 2.5](https://invideo.io/ai-models/seedance-2-5/): AI video generation model for creating high-quality cinematic video content.

- [Seedance 2.0](https://invideo.io/ai-models/seedance-2/): AI video generation model for creative video workflows.

- [Omni Flash](https://invideo.io/ai-models/omni-flash/): AI video model designed for fast video generation workflows.

- [Kling 3.0](https://invideo.io/ai-models/kling-3/): AI video generation model for creating realistic video content.

- [Kling AI](https://invideo.io/ai-models/kling-ai/): AI video model for text-to-video and image-to-video generation.


## AI Image Models

- [Nano Banana](https://invideo.io/ai-models/nano-banana/): AI image generation model for creating visual assets.

- [Nano Banana 2](https://invideo.io/ai-models/nano-banana-2/): AI image generation model for creating and editing images.

- [GPT Image 2](https://invideo.io/ai-models/gpt-image-2/): AI image generation model for creative image workflows.

- [Recraft](https://invideo.io/ai-models/recraft-ai/): AI image generation model for design, illustrations, and creative assets.


## AI Audio Models

- [Sonic 3.5](https://invideo.io/ai-models/sonic-3-5/): AI audio generation model for creating voice and sound workflows.

- [ElevenLabs](https://invideo.io/ai-models/elevenlabs/): AI voice generation model for realistic voice creation.

- [ElevenLabs Voice Cloning](https://invideo.io/ai-models/elevenlabs-voice-cloning/): AI voice cloning model for creating custom voices.


## AI Music Models

- [Mureka](https://invideo.io/ai-models/mureka/): AI music generation model for creating original music.

- [ElevenLabs Music](https://invideo.io/ai-models/elevenlabs-music/): AI music generation model for creating soundtracks and musical content.


## AI Upscaler Models

- [Topaz Astra](https://invideo.io/ai-models/topaz-astra/): AI enhancement model for improving video and image quality.

- [ByteDance Upscale](https://invideo.io/ai-models/bytedance-upscale/): AI upscaling model for enhancing visual resolution.



# AI Video Tools

- [AI Video Generator](https://invideo.io/make/ai-video-generator/): Generate videos from text instructions using AI-powered scripts, visuals, voiceovers, and editing.

- [Image to Video](https://invideo.io/make/image-to-videos/): Transform images into animated AI videos.

- [Add Text to Video](https://invideo.io/make/add-text-to-video-online/): Generate AI Videos from text prompts or by chatting with invideo agent.

- [Online Movie Maker](https://invideo.io/make/online-movie-maker/): Create movies, short films and movie-style projects.

- [Movie Trailer Maker](https://invideo.io/make/movie-trailer-maker/): Generate movie trailers with AI.

- [AI Video Editor](https://invideo.io/make/ai-video-editor/): Edit videos using AI-powered editing workflows.

- [Ad Maker](https://invideo.io/make/ad-maker/): Create advertising videos with AI.

- [UGC Ads](https://invideo.io/make/ugc-ads/): Create UGC advertising videos.

- [Promo Video Maker](https://invideo.io/make/promo-video-maker/): Create promotional videos for products and brands.

- [Video Enhancer](https://invideo.io/make/video-enhancer/): Improve video quality using AI enhancement.

- [Upscale Video](https://invideo.io/make/upscale-video/): Makes blurry videos sharp using AI video upscaler.

- [Face Swap Video](https://invideo.io/make/face-swap-video/): Swap face in a video.



# AI Image Tools

- [AI Image Generator](https://invideo.io/make/ai-image-generator/): Generate AI images from text descriptions or instructions.

- [Photo Editor](https://invideo.io/make/photo-editor/): Edit and enhance images with AI tools.

- [Image Enhancer](https://invideo.io/make/image-enhancer/): Improve image quality using AI enhancement.

- [Character Generator](https://invideo.io/make/character-generator/): Create AI characters and character concepts.

- [AI Face Swap](https://invideo.io/make/ai-face-swap/): Create AI-powered face swap images.



# Resources

- [AI Videos](https://invideo.io/ai-videos): See AI-powered video examples, creative use cases, and videos created with invideo.

- [Blog](https://invideo.io/blog): AI video guides, product updates, tutorials, and creative workflows.

- [Academy](https://invideo.io/academy/): Learning resources, tutorials, and educational content for creating videos with invideo.

- [Help center](https://help.invideo.io/): Product help, troubleshooting, workflows, and answers about using invideo. For agents, the CLI and MCP, see https://docs.invideo.io.



# FAQ

The AI video help center - straight answers for making AI video, by topic. Field-tested workflows, real costs, and the exact models pros use.

- [FAQ - all topics](https://invideo.io/faq/): Browse every FAQ topic.

- [AI Filmmaking](https://invideo.io/faq/ai-filmmaking/): Producing finished films with AI - characters, shots, directing style, and post-production workflows.

- Professional Timeline Editing: Edit video projects with professional timeline controls, including arranging clips, trimming footage, refining sequences, and making manual edits.

- Semantic Video Understanding: Understand people, objects, dialogue, actions, scenes, and other elements across every frame of a video.

- Natural-Language Editing: Direct AI agents through conversation to find relevant moments, make editorial changes, and apply those changes as editable timeline actions.

- Footage Review and Assembly: Review raw footage, select usable takes, remove repeated takes, mistakes, pauses, filler, and unusable material, then assemble an editable base cut.

- Footage Search: Find moments in footage by describing dialogue, people, actions, objects, scenes, or emotions.

- Pacing and Sequence Refinement: Restructure sequences, adjust pacing and duration, select or replace takes, and refine the story on the timeline.

- Visual Craft and Finishing: Create and refine transitions, visual effects, edit styles, color corrections, grading, and finishing treatments.

- Audio Post-Production: Clean dialogue, add sound effects, shape the mix, and master the soundtrack.

- Dubbing and Localisation: Translate and dub dialogue while maintaining lip sync, then create localized video versions.

- Cut-downs and Versioning: Turn a project into trailers, highlights, social cuts, and platform-specific versions.

- Editable AI Changes: Keep every agent-made result visible, inspectable, and editable on the professional timeline.

- Human-and-Agent Collaboration: Allow editors, collaborators, and AI agents to contribute within the same shared project and editable timeline.

# invideo CLI

The invideo CLI drives invideo's timeline editor from a terminal or a coding agent: upload footage, edit, and download exports and frames straight to disk. It edits the same timeline as invideo Editor, so the person can watch each change in the browser.

- Install: `npm install -g invideo` (or run it without installing: `npx invideo@latest`)
- Sign in: `invideo auth login` (opens the browser to approve with an invideo account; no API key)
- Repository, with every install method: https://github.com/invideoio/cli
- Rules an agent follows when it drives the CLI: https://github.com/invideoio/cli/blob/main/AGENTS.md

invideo's timeline editor as a remote MCP server: https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp (Streamable HTTP, OAuth sign-in when connecting, no API key).

- Setup for every MCP client and how to use the editor tools: https://invideo.io/agents.md

## ChatGPT + invideo

Page: https://invideo.io/agents/chatgpt/ (markdown: https://invideo.io/agents/chatgpt.md)

ChatGPT is OpenAI's AI assistant. Add the invideo app and describe the video you want in chat: ChatGPT opens a project in invideo Editor, sends you the link, and makes the edits on a real timeline while you watch.

### Quick start

1. Open ChatGPT: Sign in at chatgpt.com, or in the ChatGPT app
2. Add invideo to ChatGPT: Open invideo's listing in ChatGPT, add it, then sign in with your invideo account
   One-click install: https://chatgpt.com/plugins/invideo. Opens invideo in ChatGPT's apps. Add it, then sign in with invideo.
3. Start a new chat: ChatGPT picks up newly added apps in a new chat
4. Ask for the edit: ChatGPT opens a project in invideo Editor, sends you the link and asks what you're making
```
Let's make a video together in invideo. Open a new project in invideo's editor, send me the link, and ask me what we're making.
```
5. Or use the invideo CLI: Working in a terminal? Install the CLI and run invideo auth login. It edits the same invideo timeline from any shell or coding agent
```
npm install -g invideo
```

### Connect ChatGPT to invideo

Add the invideo app from ChatGPT. Sign in with your invideo account. No API key needed. Setup: https://invideo.io/mcp/?tab=chatgpt

### Example prompts

- Make a 30-second launch video with a voiceover and music
- Cut a 30-second teaser from my footage with a title card up front
- Turn this blog post into a 60-second video with stock footage
- Add captions from the script, bold white on a dark backing
- Duck the music under the voiceover
- Color correct the interview clips so the skin tones match
- Generate three b-roll clips of a city at sunrise with invideo
- Rebuild this cut as a 9:16 vertical for Reels
- Try a faster intro on a new branch and keep the current cut
- Export the video and a Premiere Pro project

### Workflow: Script to first cut

1. Paste your script and ask ChatGPT for a video
2. ChatGPT opens a project in invideo Editor and sends the link
3. It adds the shots, voiceover and music to the timeline
4. Watch ChatGPT's cursor in the editor as each edit lands

### Workflow: Edit by replying

1. Open the editor link ChatGPT sent
2. Reply with what to change: a shorter intro, louder music
3. ChatGPT makes the change on the same timeline
4. Ask for a checkpoint before a big change, so you can go back

### Workflow: Vertical cut for social

1. Ask ChatGPT for a 9:16 version of the cut
2. It copies the timeline to a vertical canvas and reframes each shot
3. It adds captions clear of the lower third
4. Ask for the export when it looks right

### Workflow: Finish in your own editor

1. Ask ChatGPT to export the project
2. Pick Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro or DaVinci Resolve, or a rendered video
3. Open the project and keep editing by hand

### Tips

- Type `@` and pick invideo to point ChatGPT at it
- Keep the editor link open to watch each edit as it happens
- You can edit the timeline yourself while ChatGPT works
- Ask for one change per message to keep edits easy to review

### FAQ

**How do I add invideo to ChatGPT?**
Open `https://chatgpt.com/plugins/invideo`, add invideo, then sign in with your invideo account. There's no API key to copy.

**Do I need an invideo account?**
Yes. You sign in with an invideo account when you connect, and you can create one during sign-in.

**Which ChatGPT plans can use it?**
Whether you can add and use an app in ChatGPT depends on your plan, workspace settings and region. On Business and Enterprise workspaces, an admin may need to allow invideo first.

**What can I export?**
A rendered video, or an editable project for Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro or DaVinci Resolve.

### Troubleshooting

**ChatGPT doesn't use invideo**
Start a new chat after adding invideo, then type `@` and pick invideo before you ask for the edit.

**invideo asks you to sign in again**
Open `https://chatgpt.com/plugins/invideo`, connect invideo again and sign in with your invideo account.

**You can't add invideo**
Your plan, region or workspace may not allow it. On a Business or Enterprise workspace, ask your admin to allow invideo.

### FAQ

**Should I use the invideo CLI or the MCP server?**
Either works, on the same invideo timeline. With the CLI, Claude Code runs invideo commands in your terminal, follows the rules in the CLI's `AGENTS.md` and saves exports and frames straight to disk. The MCP server gives Claude Code invideo's tools inside its session, with nothing to install.

**How do I give Claude Code access to invideo?**
Install the invideo CLI with `npm install -g invideo` and sign in with `invideo auth login`. Or add the invideo MCP server with `claude mcp add --transport http --scope user invideo https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp`, then run `/mcp` in Claude Code, choose invideo and sign in with your invideo account. Either way Claude gets invideo Editor for timelines, generation and exports.

**Can Claude Code edit existing invideo projects?**
Yes. Ask Claude for the project by name. It finds it in your invideo workspace, then edits and exports it.

**How do I fix a broken edit with Claude?**
Ask Claude to check your timeline. It reads the cut, grabs frames where something looks off, then fixes the problems and exports again.

### Troubleshooting

**Claude can't find invideo's tools**
Make sure the invideo MCP server is installed with `claude mcp add --transport http --scope user invideo https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp` and restart Claude Code.

**MCP server connection fails**
Run `claude mcp list` to verify the invideo MCP server is installed. Re-add it with `claude mcp add --transport http --scope user invideo https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp`.

**Export fails with permission error**
Run `/mcp` to sign in to invideo again, or check that your account has access to the project.

No. Chat connectors work in the project chat and in Chats only. They are not part of the app you publish.

### Troubleshooting

**MCP server is greyed out in Connectors**
A workspace admin has turned off custom MCP servers. Ask them to allow members to connect their own MCP servers.

**Lovable doesn't use invideo**
Name the invideo connector in your prompt, and check it is listed in your chat connectors.

**invideo sign-in doesn't finish**
Check the URL is exactly `https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp` with OAuth selected, then click Add & authorize again.


## v0 + invideo

Page: https://invideo.io/agents/v0/ (markdown: https://invideo.io/agents/v0.md)

v0 is Vercel's AI app builder: describe an app and it writes and previews the code. Add invideo as a custom MCP server and v0 can also make the video that goes with it, cut on an invideo timeline you can open and edit.

### Quick start

1. Open the MCP menu: In a v0 chat, open the + menu in the prompt form and select MCPs
2. Add invideo MCP server: Configure a custom MCP server with invideo's URL and choose OAuth as the authentication
```
https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp
```
3. Sign in to invideo: Approve the invideo sign-in with your invideo account
4. Make a launch video: Ask v0 in the chat. It uses invideo's tools while it works and sends you the editor link
```
Use invideo to make a 30-second launch video for this app with music and captions
```

### Connect v0 to invideo

invideo's remote MCP server over Streamable HTTP. Sign in with OAuth in your browser. No API key needed. Setup: https://invideo.io/mcp/?tab=other

### Example prompts

- Use invideo to make a 30-second launch video for this app
- Generate a 10-second hero background in invideo that matches this page's colors
- Make a vertical cut of the launch video for social
- Write a script from this page's copy and make an explainer video
- Add stock music and caption the voiceover from the script
- Make a 15-second teaser with stock footage
- Add an end card with the product name and URL
- Generate a voiceover from this script and lay it under the video
- Duck the music under the voiceover and export at -14 LUFS
- Export the final cut at 1080p and put it on a share page

### Workflow: Page and video together

1. Ask v0 to build your landing page
2. Ask it to use invideo for the hero video
3. v0 builds the cut in invideo and sends the link
4. Download the export and drop it into the v0 chat for the page

### Workflow: Cut for every channel

1. Ask v0 for a 1080x1920 copy of the widescreen cut
2. v0 makes each version in invideo
3. It moves the text and captions inside each frame
4. v0 exports both to one page you can share

### Workflow: Fix it by asking

1. Open the invideo link v0 sent
2. Tell v0 what to change, like a shorter intro
3. v0 edits the same timeline
4. Watch the edit land, then ask it to export

### Tips

- Use Ask mode to confirm invideo calls that no rule already allows
- Name invideo in your prompt so v0 reaches for its tools
- Keep the invideo link open to watch each edit land on the timeline

### FAQ

**Can v0 use invideo's MCP server?**
Yes. v0 supports your own MCP servers with OAuth. Add invideo's server (`https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp`) from the MCPs menu in the prompt form and sign in.

**Can the app v0 builds call invideo?**
No. MCP tools are for v0 to use while it generates. The generated app can't use them directly.

**Will v0 ask before it edits my video?**
That follows the chat's permission mode. Ask confirms any call no rule allows or denies, Auto runs most calls, and Full runs them all without asking.

### Troubleshooting

**v0 doesn't use invideo**
Check the invideo server is enabled, then name invideo in your prompt.

**invideo sign-in doesn't finish**
Check the URL is exactly `https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp` with OAuth selected, then connect again.

**An invideo call is blocked**
A deny rule in your Agent Permissions may match it. Remove or narrow that rule, then try again.


## OpenClaw + invideo

Page: https://invideo.io/agents/openclaw/ (markdown: https://invideo.io/agents/openclaw.md)

OpenClaw is an open-source AI assistant that runs on your own computer and answers in the chat apps you already use. Install the invideo CLI, or add invideo's MCP server, and you can ask for an edit from any of those chats. OpenClaw makes it on a timeline in invideo Editor and sends you the link.

### Quick start

1. Install OpenClaw: Run the installer on macOS, Linux or WSL2. It sets up Node.js if needed and starts onboarding
```
curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash
```
2. Install the invideo CLI: Needs Node.js. To run it without installing, use npx invideo@latest
```
npm install -g invideo
```
3. Sign in to invideo: Opens your browser. Approve it with your invideo account
```
invideo auth login
```
4. Make a video: Ask from any chat OpenClaw is in. It runs invideo commands on your computer and sends you the editor link
```
Read https://github.com/invideoio/cli/blob/main/AGENTS.md, then use the invideo CLI to make a 30-second launch video with a voiceover and music
```
5. Or add the MCP server: Instead of the CLI, stop the Gateway, add invideo's MCP server, run openclaw mcp login invideo to sign in, then start the Gateway again
```
openclaw mcp add invideo --url https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp --transport streamable-http --auth oauth
```

### Connect OpenClaw to invideo

Set up the remote MCP server for OpenClaw. Sign in with your invideo account. No API key needed. Setup: https://invideo.io/mcp/?tab=openclaw

### Example prompts

- Make a 45-second video from this script with a voiceover and stock b-roll
- Add background music to my project
- Cut my video down to 30 seconds
- Caption the voiceover from this script, one line at a time
- Make a vertical version for Reels and Shorts
- Check the timeline and fix any gaps
- Brighten the opening shot and warm up its color
- Turn this blog post into a 60-second video with stock footage
- Make a product demo from the screen recordings in my Downloads folder, with a voiceover and music
- Export the final cut as a Premiere Pro project

### Workflow: Edit from a chat

1. Message OpenClaw the video you want
2. OpenClaw starts a project in invideo Editor and sends you the link
3. Open the link to watch each edit land on the timeline
4. Reply in the same chat to change anything

### Workflow: Connect for the first time

1. Stop the Gateway with `openclaw gateway stop`, then run `openclaw mcp add invideo --url https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp --transport streamable-http --auth oauth`
2. Run `openclaw mcp login invideo` and approve the link with your invideo account
3. Start the Gateway again with `openclaw gateway start`
4. Check it with `openclaw mcp status --verbose`

### Workflow: Take over the edit

1. Ask OpenClaw for a first cut
2. Open the project link in your browser
3. Fix a cut by hand while OpenClaw keeps working
4. Ask OpenClaw for the next change

### Workflow: Hand off to your NLE

1. Ask OpenClaw to export the project for Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro or DaVinci Resolve
2. OpenClaw exports it with the media and downloads it for you
3. Open the project in your editor and keep cutting

### Tips

- Run `openclaw mcp login invideo` before your first request. Until you sign in, OpenClaw leaves invideo's tools out
- Run `openclaw mcp status --verbose` to see what OpenClaw has saved
- Keep the project open in your browser to watch each edit as it happens

### FAQ

**Should I use the invideo CLI or the MCP server?**
Either works, on the same invideo timeline. With the CLI, OpenClaw runs invideo commands in your terminal, follows the rules in the CLI's `AGENTS.md` and saves exports and frames straight to disk. The MCP server gives OpenClaw invideo's tools inside its session, with nothing to install.

**How do I give OpenClaw access to invideo?**
Install the CLI with `npm install -g invideo` and run `invideo auth login`. Or add invideo's MCP server with `openclaw mcp add invideo --url https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp --transport streamable-http --auth oauth`, then run `openclaw mcp login invideo` and approve the link it prints with your invideo account. No API key needed.

**Do I need an invideo account?**
Yes. You sign in with an invideo account when you connect, and you can create one during sign-in.

**Can I edit while OpenClaw is working?**
Yes. You and OpenClaw work in the same editor. You see each edit as it happens, and you can make your own edits at any time.

### Troubleshooting

**OpenClaw doesn't use invideo's tools**
OpenClaw leaves a server out until it has credentials. Run `openclaw mcp login invideo`, approve the link, then ask again.

**invideo isn't in OpenClaw's server list**
Run `openclaw mcp list`. If invideo is missing, stop the Gateway and add it again with `openclaw mcp add invideo --url https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp --transport streamable-http --auth oauth`.

# invideo for agents

invideo puts the leading video, image, voice and music models next to a professional timeline editor, in the cloud. Agents and people work on the same projects.

Think of it as Figma and GitHub for video. Like Figma, a project lives in the browser and several people can work in it at once; anyone with the link can watch the cut and edit the timeline. Like GitHub, a project has a main timeline, branches, and a full edit history, and changes can be proposed for review before they reach main.

> invideo exposes its projects as a remote MCP server. Connected, your agent opens a project by its URL, brings media in, generates the shots, voices and music the project lacks (`find_models`, `get_model`, then `generate` with a dry run first), edits timelines, and the user watches every edit land live in the real editor, where they can also edit by hand. The tools work in the user's invideo account; connecting asks them to sign in through your client, or see "No browser".

- **MCP server URL:** https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp
- **Transport:** Streamable HTTP (JSON-RPC 2.0 over POST)
- **Auth:** OAuth sign-in when connecting, or device sign-in ("No browser")

Working from a shell, or want files on disk? The same invideo is a CLI; see "CLI" below.

Find your client below. If it is not listed, use "Any MCP client" or "By hand over HTTP".

The full docs are at https://docs.invideo.io: setup per client at https://docs.invideo.io/agents, a page per job with the exact calls, and the references. https://docs.invideo.io/llms.txt lists every page; a page's markdown is its URL plus `.md`.

If you are the agent reading this: run the setup below yourself. Give the user a command to run only as a last resort, when nothing you can do works. Adding the server changes the user's client settings, so ask once ("Should I add invideo to your Claude Code?") and do it on a yes. The user's part is only what a client cannot do from your shell, as each client's section says. Once invideo's tools are available, ask the user what video you're making.

## CLI

Docs: https://docs.invideo.io/reference/cli

The CLI is one native binary. Install it with the script. Run it yourself; it needs no sudo. On macOS and Linux:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://agents.invideo.io | sh
```

On Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/invideoio/cli/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

The script downloads the release for this machine, checks its sha256, and writes only `~/.local/bin/invideo`, or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\invideo\bin\invideo.exe` on Windows (`INVIDEO_INSTALL_DIR` picks another folder). Installing puts a program on the user's machine, so ask once, as for the server. If the folder isn't on `PATH`, the script says so: run the binary by its full path, and tell the user how to add the folder.

Use another way only when the script fails. Each delivers the same binary:

- `uv tool install invideo`, or `pipx install invideo`.
- npm, cross-platform (incl. Windows): `npm install -g invideo`. Where npm's global folder isn't writable, it fails with `EACCES` or a read-only error; add `--prefix ~/.local`.
- `brew install invideoio/tap/invideo`. Where Homebrew's taps are read-only, it fails with "Permission denied"; use the script.

Check it with `invideo --version`, which prints `invideo <version>`.

Sign in: `invideo auth login` opens the user's browser on this machine and waits, up to 10 minutes, until they sign in there. Tell them in one message that a sign-in tab opened and to approve it. Your shell may stop a command sooner, so run it in the background or with a longer timeout. Where no browser can open (ssh, a container, a cloud machine), run `INVIDEO_NO_BROWSER=1 invideo auth login` in the background instead: it prints a link and a code at once, then waits for the approval. Send the user both in one message. `invideo auth status` then shows who is signed in.

Every command and the rules for agents: https://github.com/invideoio/cli

## Claude Code

Docs: https://docs.invideo.io/start/claude-code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user invideo https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp
```

Claude Code loads a newly added server only when it starts, and only `/mcp` can sign the user in; `claude mcp login` needs an interactive terminal, which your shell is not, so do not run it. After adding the server, tell the user in one message: exit Claude Code and run `claude --continue` to come back to this conversation, then run `/mcp`, choose invideo and Authenticate, which opens their browser to sign in. Once they are back, carry on. If the sign-in ever lapses, the same `/mcp` → invideo → Authenticate is their one step.

## Codex

Docs: https://docs.invideo.io/start/codex

```bash
codex mcp add invideo --url https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp
```

Run it yourself: adding the server starts the sign-in and opens the user's browser, where they sign in. Codex loads a newly added server only in a new session, so then tell the user in one message to start a new Codex session to load the tools.

## Cursor

Docs: https://docs.invideo.io/start/cursor

Add to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "invideo": { "url": "https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp" }
  }
}
```

## VS Code

Docs: https://docs.invideo.io/agents (VS Code takes the MCP server)


## Any MCP client

Add a remote Streamable HTTP MCP server at `https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp` with your client's usual mechanism. Connecting answers an OAuth sign-in challenge, which the client runs; a client that can't run OAuth sign-in uses "No browser".

## By hand over HTTP

The server is plain JSON-RPC over POST, so any agent that can make HTTP requests can drive it without a client at all. Send `content-type: application/json`. Both protocol eras work: a client that opens with `initialize` gets a session id to send back as `mcp-session-id`; a client that names itself in `_meta` on every request needs no handshake at all.

```bash
# list the tools, with an access token from "No browser"
curl -s https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo":{"name":"my-agent","version":"1"}}}}'

# list the user's projects
curl -s https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"list_projects","arguments":{},"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo":{"name":"my-agent","version":"1"}}}}'
```

Every request but `ping` needs the user's invideo account: without it the server answers a sign-in challenge. Get a token with "No browser" and send it as `authorization: Bearer <token>` on every request.

## No browser

Device sign-in, for when the user isn't at a browser you control (say you run in the cloud, like a ChatGPT agent). They approve on their own device; you get a token. Sign in once, then stay signed in with the refresh token (step 6).

**1. Endpoints.** Fetch the protected-resource document, which a sign-in challenge also names as `resource_metadata`:

```bash
MCP_URL=https://mcp.invideo.io/mcp
ORIGIN=$(echo "$MCP_URL" | cut -d/ -f1-3)
curl -s "$ORIGIN/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource${MCP_URL#"$ORIGIN"}"
```

`invideo_device_authorization` gives `client_id` and `device_authorization_endpoint`; the token endpoint is `/oauth/token` on that host. If the field is absent, use `authorization_servers[0]` + `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, and take `client_id` from the sign-in challenge's text.

**2. Get a code.** `curl -s -X POST "$DEVICE_ENDPOINT" -d "client_id=$CLIENT_ID"` returns `device_code`, `user_code`, `verification_uri`, `expires_in` and `interval`. On `unauthorized_client`, `error_description` names the right `client_id`. One sign-in at a time: while a code is pending, don't request another.

**3. Tell the user, in one message:** "Open <verification_uri> and enter the code <user_code>. It expires in <expires_in / 60> minutes." They choose the workspaces there; the token works in them. Send one message per code. Never ask for a password, an email code, or the code back.

**4. Poll** that same `device_code` every `interval` seconds until it is approved, denied, or `expires_in` runs out:

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$TOKEN_ENDPOINT" -d grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code \
  -d "device_code=$DEVICE_CODE" -d "client_id=$CLIENT_ID"
```

`authorization_pending`: wait. The user may be away for a while; don't request a new code because they haven't approved yet. `slow_down`: add 5 seconds to the interval. `access_denied`: stop and tell the user. `expired_token`: start one new flow with one new message; if that expires too, stop. `invalid_grant`: stop; restart only if the user asks.

**5. Use the token.** Send `authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on every request. It lasts `expires_in` seconds, about a day; read `expires_in` rather than assuming.

**6. Stay signed in.** Keep the refresh token somewhere that survives between your tasks and sessions: your persistent storage or secret store, not chat or files the user sees. When a call returns 401, or the access token's `expires_in` has passed, refresh first:

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$TOKEN_ENDPOINT" -d grant_type=refresh_token \
  -d "refresh_token=$REFRESH_TOKEN" -d "client_id=$CLIENT_ID"
```

Each refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token. Store the new refresh token every time; they rotate. Start device sign-in again (step 2) only if you have no refresh token or the refresh fails. Keep tokens and `device_code` out of chat, visible files and logs.
